title: Agent Registry vs. Agent Inventory
summary: Two records, two jobs, and one system that cannot do both. How each gets populated, what the shipping tools actually collect, and the reconciliation query that tells you how much of your estate is ungoverned.
body_markdown:
TL;DR


**Inventory and registry are sequential records, not rival names for one thing. One is populated by scanners and has to include what nobody approved; the other is populated by a review and must not.**


The federal government publishes a working example of the ratio. The 2025 consolidation of agency AI use-case inventories under OMB Memorandum M-25-21 covers 56 agencies and 3,611 reported use cases, of which 445 are designated high-impact. Broad record, narrow subset, both published.


The confusion is understandable, because the tools use the words interchangeably. Microsoft's own documentation calls its agent registry a place that "can contain a large and diverse inventory of agents", and surfaces a counter for agents "created or managed outside of Agent 365". That counter is an inventory fact sitting inside a registry.


We are not arguing for more process. The inventory should stay wide, cheap and automatic. The registry should stay narrow and deliberate.


The useful artifact is the diff between them, run as a scheduled query rather than a quarterly slide: discovered but not registered, registered but not discovered, and registered with wider access than the entry says.
